title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Chips Paddle Back Out, Dow Stays on the Sand
conditions.summary: Nasdaq and the S&P 500 bounced as AI and chip stocks recovered part of Thursday's rout, while the Dow slipped. A strong October jobs report pushed yields and the dollar higher, and the S&P still logged its worst week since June.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: S&P 500 closed at 7,376.86, up 0.31%; Nasdaq Composite at 24,579.42, up 1.09%; Dow at 51,285.73, down 0.46%; Russell 2000 up about 0.9%.
AI and chip stocks rebounded after Thursday's selloff, when the S&P 500 fell more than 4% and the chip index dropped 12%.
The Dow opened down nearly 1% while the S&P 500 was up as much as about 1.5% around midday before fading.
Technology and communication services led; consumer staples, health care and financials lagged.
The S&P 500 still had its worst week since June, and tech stocks fell about 7% for the week.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: October payrolls rose 165,000 versus about 65,000 expected; unemployment fell to 4.1% versus 4.2% expected.
Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% for the month and 3.1% from a year ago; August and September were revised up a combined 84,000.
The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 2 basis points to roughly 4.86%; the 2-year rose about 4.5 basis points to 4.52%.
The dollar index gained about 0.75% to 102.32, and bets on a December Fed rate hike increased after the report.
Investors weighed midterm results that could bring tighter rules on AI data-center construction.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: AMD (Advanced Micro Devices): up roughly 8% to 10% — rebound after a 17% drop Thursday.
NVDA (Nvidia): higher — chip bounce after a 9% slide Thursday.
ABNB (Airbnb): about +12% midday — strong quarter, raised full-year outlook and new buyback.
NET (Cloudflare): about +13% early — strong third-quarter results and guidance.
HIMS (Hims & Hers): about +5% — Eli Lilly will let it sell Zepbound and Foundayo directly.
DKNG (DraftKings): about -28% early — third-quarter miss.
AXON (Axon Enterprise): about -18% midday — earnings miss and lower 2026 outlook.
TEAM (Atlassian): about -14% early — guidance pointed to a sharp growth slowdown.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Airbnb, Cloudflare, Atlassian, DraftKings and Axon reported last night and set the tone for today's moves.
Microchip fell about 13% midday after analysts cut forecasts following its report.
Natera fell about 12% early on a wider loss and a CEO change.
About 440 S&P 500 companies have now reported this season; no major names reported after Friday's close.

sections.title: Business News
items: Salesforce agreed to buy voice-AI company Cresta for a reported $2.7 billion.
Meta acquired AI agent startup Conductor; terms were not disclosed.
Eli Lilly will let Hims & Hers sell its weight-loss drugs Zepbound and Foundayo directly.
Tesla plans to wind down Cybertruck production in Texas around mid-2027 to make room for Cybercab.
Reports said Anthropic's IPO valuation could come in below earlier projections.

sections.title: On Deck
items: Markets are closed for the weekend; next session is Monday, Nov 9.
Monday Fed speakers: Bowman 7:40 AM CT, Goolsbee 9:00 AM CT, Barkin 11:15 AM CT; wholesale inventories at 9:00 AM CT.
Monday before the open: KKR, Constellation Energy, Ferguson and Barrick; after the close: Take-Two Interactive and Rocket Lab.
Tuesday 7:30 AM CT: October CPI, the big data release of the week.

Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Friday, November sixth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding into the water for the last set of the week.

Gus the wonder dog is curled up on his beach towel after a rough week. Gus, tell everybody we made it to Friday! [BARK]

Okay, the Final Set. After Thursday's gnarly wipeout in A I and chip stocks, the swell came back in, but not for everybody. The S and P five hundred rose about three tenths of a percent to seven thousand three hundred seventy six. The Nasdaq Composite gained about one point one percent to twenty four thousand five hundred seventy nine. The Dow slipped about half a percent to fifty one thousand two hundred eighty six. The Russell two thousand rose almost nine tenths of a percent. Tech and communication services led the way, while consumer staples, health care and financials pulled back. Still, the S and P had its worst week since June.

Over in the bond lineup, the ten year Treasury yield rose about two basis points to roughly four point eight six percent. The dollar index climbed about three quarters of a percent. W T I crude settled near ninety one dollars. Gold fell about one percent to around four thousand seventy five dollars. The VIX fear gauge dropped about nine percent.

Now the Wind and Weather. The October jobs report blew in strong. Employers added one hundred sixty five thousand jobs, way above forecasts near sixty five thousand. Unemployment slipped to four point one percent, and wages rose four tenths of a percent for the month. Yields jumped on the news, and traders raised their bets on a Fed rate hike in December. Investors also worry new rules after the midterms could slow A I data center building.

Time for the Lineup. Advanced Micro Devices bounced roughly eight to ten percent after a seventeen percent drop on Thursday. Nvidia came back too. Airbnb was up about twelve percent at midday after a strong quarter, a raised outlook and a new buyback. Cloudflare surged on strong results and guidance. That's catching a clean wave and riding it all the way to the beach. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! [SNACK]

On the wipeout side, DraftKings sank more than twenty five percent after missing estimates. Axon fell about eighteen percent on a miss and a lower outlook.

On the Tide Chart, this week's earnings parade is winding down, with about four hundred forty S and P companies already reported. Friday evening was quiet.

Beach Talk. Salesforce agreed to buy voice A I company Cresta for about two point seven billion dollars. Meta picked up A I agent startup Conductor. Eli Lilly will let Hims and Hers sell its weight loss drugs Zepbound and Foundayo, and Hims stock hung ten on that news.

Tomorrow's Forecast is really Monday. Fed speakers Bowman, Goolsbee and Barkin all take the mic. Before the open, we hear from K K R and Constellation Energy. After the close, Take-Two Interactive and Rocket Lab report. And Tuesday at seven thirty A M Central, the October consumer price report lands. That's the big wave of the week.

Got a stock, E T F or futures contract on your mind? Look it up in the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. Wax those boards this weekend and catch Dawn Patrol on Monday morning, Soul Surfers.

This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
